output.summary: KEP-714 proposes replacing the monolithic kubernetes-test.tar.gz release artifact with several platform-specific test tarballs, one per platform in KUBE_TEST_PLATFORMS, matching the existing client/node/server tarball pattern. Status is implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: The single "mondo" test tarball kept growing as platforms were added (about 1.2GB at v1.13.2, 1.3-1.5GB in earlier releases). Users who only need one platform must download everything, and Bazel cross-compilation of multiple targets in one call is poorly supported, which made producing identical Bazel and non-Bazel artifacts harder. Splitting the tarball by platform addresses both problems.

alternatives.why_not: The tarball had grown to roughly 1.2GB to 1.5GB as platforms increased, which is the problem the KEP sets out to solve.

alternatives.option: Change the underlying build system (make/shell or Bazel)
alternatives.why_not: The non-goals state that the build system is not changed; both build systems are affected but users keep their existing workflow.

alternatives.option: Prune unused binaries and portable sources from the test tarballs
alternatives.why_not: Removing cruft is an explicit non-goal; the sources say pruning will not happen with this effort.

alternatives.option: Make test binaries directly downloadable from GCS
alternatives.why_not: Changing what is released independent of the test tarball is an explicit non-goal.

evidence.quote: This KEP proposes replacing the monolith test tarball with platform-specific tarballs, matching the existing pattern used for the client, node, and server tarballs.
As of Kubernetes v1.13.2, the official `kubernetes-test.tar.gz` is approximately 1.2GB; previous releases ranged from 1.3 - 1.5GB.
combining multiple target platforms in one Bazel call is currently not well-supported. Separating this tarball would make it easier
Instead of building and distributing a single `kubernetes-test.tar.gz` with all portable sources and compiled binaries for all platforms, produce several platform-specific tarballs
